posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
On saving money by buying during the Kickstarter: Yes, you'll save money ON THE RETAIL PRICE. Often, though, products are sold at a discount from wholesalers. Combine that with the ability to possibly save on shipping by getting many products from the same wholesaler, and it is far from guaranteed that the Kickstarter is the best way to get the very best price.

 

There are some things in this Kickstarter that you will have difficulty getting other places:

  • The new promo cards: Yes, you'd be able to later order the Hero Variant Collection, and thus get all of the cards, BUT the art on the new promos available via this Kickstarter is going to be different than the art in the Hero Variant Collection. So if you care about that and are not planning on being at a convention where GtG has a booth, this may be the only way to get _those_ cards with _that_ art save from buying them on eBay. Once you go the eBay route, you'd probably be saving money via the Kickstarter
  • The Canvas print: Apologies if I've missed it, but it's not clear that the canvas print will be available after the Kickstarter. My guess is that if lots of people want to buy this in the future that GtG would do create more, but I think it's more likely that they'll get enough to fulfill Kickstarter orders and maybe a bit more, and then this will become unavailable.
  • The Ultimate Collector's Box: They'll probably keep this in stock in their own web store, but it may be something that retailers aren't interested in and therefore distributors and wholesalers don't end up carrying it, so even if it _is_ available, it probably won't be available at a discount.

 

If your main interest is to get all of the cards and you don't care about having every single piece of art, and you don't need an extra box or a canvas print, AND YOU DON'T MIND possibly getting your games/cards later than other people, then you may have no particular need to order via the Kickstarter and can likely get a better price later.

 

Now, most of us may want you to order via the Kickstarter to help us get the total up to the unrevealed stretch goals, but don't kid yourself that you're saving money.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

Just for reference I asked Christopher his expectations funding wise for OblivAeon and this was his response:

I had a good feeling that we would fund. Maybe even in the first week. I had a reasonable hope that we would break $100k, and thought that maybe, JUST MAYBE, we might break $200k. But that seemed highly unlikely.

This comes up time and again: Kickstarters like this one, or MST3K, or anything made by an established miniatures company, which seem totally assured to reach some absurdly high result.  I mean, I (obviously) don't have access to >G's financial information, but given the scope of the project, I'd have bet on this Kickstarter doing at least twice as well as Shattered Timelines, and probably closer to three times as well.  Now, obviously, that $360-545K estimate also fell far short of reality, but it's closer to the current total than to Christopher's guesses.

 

It seems like there's this strong trend among KS creators to be very conservative in their estimates.  I don't know whether this out of fear of somehow "jynxing" the results, or just humility, or what - I would have expected more overly-ambitious guesses if anything, but that's overwhelmingly not what I see.

 

I don't really have a conclusion to this - it's just some thoughts I was musing on.  In any case, a big congratulations to the whole >G team!  Try not to get buried in the avalanche of success (and work) descending upon you.
